Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $500 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

activity related to new multifamily residential, commercial, and park projects planned in the
current contract term. Amendment No. 1 was approved administratively in the amount of $39,400

of the agreement currently set at a maximum annual compensation at $189,400. The plan check
services from SFA is provided at the rate of 65% of the City’s fee schedule or hourly costs related
to the project. Because of the high volume of building related activity expected an amendment
to the agreement is proposed not-to-exceed $250,000 annually.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 25-45 - BUDGET AMENDMENT FOR MICROTRANSIT/ON-
  DEMAND PILOT TRANSIT SERVICES

Background:

The Norwalk Transit System (NTS) currently operates six Fixed Routes serving the City of
Norwalk and surrounding communities of Artesia, Bellflower, Cerritos, El Monte, La Mirada, La
Habra, Santa Fe Springs, South El Monte, Whittier and portions of unincorporated Los Angeles
County (See Exhibit I Route 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 & 7).

Fixed-Route Service Productivity:

In Fiscal Year 2024/25, NTS Fixed-Route system transported approximately 1.3 million
passengers. The highest performing most productive service includes the following Fixed-
Routes:

  •  Route 1 operates north and southbound with a southbound terminus in the City of
  Bellflower and northbound terminus at Rio Hondo College; and

  •  Route 2 operates circulator service between the Los Cerritos Mall and C Line Ligh Rail
  Station in the City of Norwalk; and

  •  Route 4 operates eastbound and westbound between the City of La Habra and C Line
  Light Rail Station via Imperial Hwy.; and

  •  Route 7 operates north and southbound with a southbound terminus at the C Line Light
  Rail Station and northbound terminus at the El Monte Bus Station.

These four Fixed-Routes had an average daily ridership of 15 passengers per hour at an average
cost of $12.00 per passenger hour.

The lowest performing service that operated on a subpar productivity basis include the following
Fixed-Routes:

  •  Route 3 operates as a local circulator with a southern terminus at 166 Street & Norwalk
  Blvd and northern terminus at the Santa Fe Springs Gateway Plaza; and

  •  Route 5 operates eastbound and westbound between the City of La Mirada and C Line
  Light Rail Station via Rosecrans Blvd.

These two Fixed-Routes had an average daily ridership of 8.9 passengers per hour at an average
cost of approximately $19.81 per passenger per hour.

Route 3 and Route 5 present several key productivity challenges as it relates to operating on
corridors that are located in low density areas with pockets of high-density housing. Also, these
routes provide limited access to major transit hubs with a few exceptions and have high headways
of 45-60 minutes with no weekend service.

To address the challenges associated with Routes 3 and 5 while preserving fixed-route service
in low-income and disadvantaged neighborhoods NTS proposes a one-year pilot of a
Microtransit/On-Demand service along the corridors currently served by these routes.

NTS will collaborate and contract with Nomad Transit, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Via
Transportation, Inc. (“Via”) for the initiation of a Microtransit/On-Demand Pilot project with a 12-
month duration following a launch date in January 2026. Via’s experience includes providing
Microtransit/On-Demand services to LA Metro, Los Angeles Department of Transportation and
Torrance Transit.

Microtransit/On-Demand Service Parameters:

Microtransit/On-Demand services allow patrons to schedule trips via a mobile app or landline.
Within a designated geographic zone, riders can request the following types of trips:

  1. Door-to-door service;
  2. Door-to-transfer service, connecting to a fixed-route public transit system, including NTS;
  3. Door-to-terminus service, with drop-off at either the Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs Metrolink
  Station or the I-105/I-605 Norwalk C Line Light Rail Station

This model relies on dynamic routing that leverages a mobile app to provide efficient
transportation that adapts to passenger needs and solves first-mile, last-mile requirements.

Although fixed-route services remain a vital option particularly in moderately dense areas with
centralized destinations, the introduction of Microtransit/On-Demand services through a contract
with Via offers significant benefits that can enhance overall system productivity. These benefits
include greater flexibility, shorter wait times, and more inclusive service options. While rideshare

partnerships such as Uber and Lyft offer a high level of user convenience, they can be cost-
prohibitive and may present accessibility challenges for individuals with disabilities if proper
accommodations are not in place.

Via will provide access to an app platform service through which patrons will be able to book and
pay for rides on a shared and on-demand basis using dedicated vehicles. Via will provide access
to booking trips by means of a dedicated phone line for patrons who do not have access to a
smartphone.

Geographic Coverage Zone:

NTS has identified corridors to better connect residents and transit users to various destinations
within a geographic zone by means of Microtransit/On-Demand service. The geographic zone
replicates corridors currently served by NTS Route 3 and NTS Route 5 Fixed-Route service.
Approximately 13.4 square miles coverage zone.

Service Days/Hours:

Monday through Friday 6:00am to 7:00pm

Fare Policy:

The Microtransit/On-Demand fare policy will be the same as NTS Fixed-Route service adult base
fare of $1.25 for duration of the Pilot Program. NTS shall collect and retain all revenue from
Microtransit/On-Demand fares, net of service fees, starting upon launch of the Pilot.

Driver Workforce & Supply Management:

Via drivers (Driver Partners) will provide transportation services to patrons through the app
Platform. Via will engage in a good faith effort to register Norwalk, CA residents as Driver
Partners.

Via will ensure that Driver Partners have appropriate licenses, permits, and insurance required
for the type of vehicles being operated. As part of Driver Partner registration for access to the
Platform, all Driver Partners will be introduced to Via regarding the following areas:

  •  Familiarization with the Pilot service area;
  •  Hours of service; Customer’s expectations;
  •  Use of the Driver App; and
  •  Reporting incidents and delays in service.

Via will be responsible for ensuring that there is adequate driver supply for the geographic service
zone within designated hours to meet demand with optimal quality of service.

Vehicle Fleet:

Via will provide a fleet of up to 15 branded, licensed, and insured vehicles, including 5 Wheelchair
Accessible Vehicles (WAVs), available for passenger use. If the branded fleet is insufficient to
meet service demand for any reason, Via has the flexibility to:

  •  Supplement the fleet with a temporary mix of other makes and models, and/or
  •  Deploy Driver Partners using their personal vehicles for short-term periods as needed to
  increase vehicle availability. These vehicles may be unbranded but will be identified with
  magnetic signage.

Via will also ensure that all necessary registrations and licensing are completed to operate the
service in compliance with applicable regulations.

Promotion & Marketing:

NTS shall provide Via with a detailed marketing plan for the portions of marketing that the
Customer is leading at least 4 weeks before the launch of the service. Via and NTS will work
collaboratively to refine the plan as needed. For clarity, Via may also choose to implement similar
marketing initiatives on behalf of NTS at its own expense. In such cases, Via will coordinate with
NTS in advance to ensure alignment and consistency.

Background:

In December 2024, an Agreement of Purchase and Sale and Initial Escrow Instruction was
entered into by the City and State of California (“State”) through its Department of General
Services for the former California Youth Authority. The site is comprised of approximately 32
acres together with improvements of approximately 35-40 structures and ancillary improvements
located at 13200 Bloomfield Avenue (“Property”). Escrow closed on July 28, 2025, for the surplus
Property pursuant to the provisions of California Assembly Bill No. 518, Chapter 43, Statutes of
2020 (“Special Legislation”). The project will create a Transit Oriented Development within the
City’s Economic Development Node No. 6.

The City also entered into a Disposition and Development Agreement with Lewis Land
Developers, LLC (“Lewis”), in December 2024. The City worked with Lewis to obtain State
approval of the Special Legislation, and to meet and negotiate with the State for the City’s
purchase of the Property, conducted extensive site investigations of the Property to determine
its feasibility for development and the extent of all environmental remediation work required for
development, undertook comprehensive stakeholder and community outreach and visionary
programs to solicit ideas for future development of the Property, designed a Transit Oriented
Development project consistent with the results of the outreach efforts that meets mobility and
greenhouse gas reduction goals and affordable housing goals of the City, and helped prepare
and process for approvals by the City Planning Commission and City Council all of the
entitlements for the project (Norwalk Transit Village Specific Plan). The City is working closely
with the Lewis team to facilitate next steps for the Property.

On July 14, 2025, the City issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 26-827, for Construction
Management Services. The construction manager will assist the City during the abatement
demolition and remediation operations of the Property. Eighteen firms attended the mandatory
pre-bid meeting on July 24, 2025. On August 21, 2025, the City received eight proposals. The
following is a list of the firms:

1.  APSI Construction Management
2.  Cumming Management Group
3.  Griffin Structures
4.  MARRS Services, Inc.
5.  Psomas
6.  Southstar Engineering and Consulting, Inc.
7.  Transtech Engineers
8.  Willdan Engineering

The evaluation committee was comprised of the Community Development Department’s Building
and Safety Division and Public Services Department’s Engineering Division staff that reviewed
and evaluated the proposals based on understating of the Project requirements, proposed scope
of work, experience of the firm and personnel, past performance and costs. The four highest
rated proposals were interviewed. After the interviews were conducted the firms ranked as
follows:

1.  Cumming Management Group
2.  Griffin Structures
3.  Willdan Engineering
4.  MARRS Services, Inc.

The Cumming Management Group (CMG) ranked number one based upon the firm’s experience
on working with public clients and serving as the owner’s representatives helping manage
projects from conception to occupancy. They have managed several similar developer/public
agency projects that include market-rate and affordable housing, community benefit space,
parks/open space, and commercial/office space. CMG has completed similar services for the
County of Los Angeles (County), including the Helen Keller Community Center project completed
in 2015, Rancho Los Amigos South Campus Remediation completed in 2023, and Demolition of
Stoneview Nature Center project completed in 2017. They also led a team of evaluators to
analyze the CYA Property at the time of the contract in 2015; the site was owned by the State
and had been determined to be excess property and was available for purchase and/or ground
lease for development.

The proposed cost for the construction management services requested is $398,690. The firm’s
team includes a Civil Engineer with expertise in construction management, project management,
and public agency capital project management and an Architect with 25 years of experience,
and a strong background in leading, managing, and coordinating a wide range of projects and
programs. They have not proposed any subconsultants for this contract. Additional costs related
to the site maintenance and security are included in the budget request for the project. Costs

Fiscal Impact:

Resolution No. 25-46 would authorize an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Adopted
Budget to appropriate $355,861 Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset funds and $533,791
Non-Housing Bond will fund the advancement of Property costs related to the ongoing security
and maintenance of the Property and the cost of a construction manager to oversee the
demolition, abatement, and remediation of the Property. Property security and maintenance
costs and construction manager costs associated with the demolition of the Property advanced
by the City will be reimbursed by Lewis in accordance with a mutually approved budget. The
cost of the construction manager overseeing abatement and remediation shall be reimbursed to
the City from State funds currently held in escrow for such purpose.
